faqs.question: What is the best time to take the Culture & Sensitivity, Aerobic bacteria Blood Two bottle set?
faqs.answer: Your doctor may advise the best collection time based on your fever pattern and symptoms. In many suspected bloodstream infections, blood is collected before starting antibiotics whenever clinically possible.

faqs.question: Is overnight fasting mandatory for the Culture & Sensitivity, Aerobic bacteria Blood Two bottle set, and for how long?
faqs.answer: No, overnight fasting is not required. You can eat and drink normally unless your doctor has advised fasting for another test being done at the same time.

faqs.question: Can dehydration affect my Culture & Sensitivity, Aerobic bacteria Blood Two bottle set results?
faqs.answer: Mild dehydration usually does not directly affect bacterial culture results. However, you should maintain normal hydration unless your doctor has restricted fluids.

faqs.question: How should I prepare my diet and medications before the Culture & Sensitivity, Aerobic bacteria Blood Two bottle set?
faqs.answer: No special diet is needed. Inform your doctor if you are taking antibiotics or have recently taken antibiotics, as this may affect bacterial growth in culture.

faqs.question: How is the blood draw procedure performed for the Culture & Sensitivity, Aerobic bacteria Blood Two bottle set?
faqs.answer: A healthcare professional cleans the puncture site, collects blood using a sterile needle into the required culture bottle or vacutainer, removes the needle and applies a bandage.

faqs.question: Are there any risks to the test?
faqs.answer: The risks are minimal and similar to a routine blood test. You may feel slight pain, mild bruising, swelling or temporary discomfort at the needle site.

faqs.question: What does no growth mean in the Culture & Sensitivity, Aerobic bacteria Blood Two bottle set?
faqs.answer: No growth means aerobic bacteria were not detected in the blood sample during the culture period. Your doctor will interpret this along with your symptoms, antibiotic history and other test results.
